title: Overspill forwarding and proportional throttling for reserved-tier quotas
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem statement: Reserved-tier tenants sometimes underutilize committed tokens while other tenants in the same organization experience transient bursts. Current behavior clips requests at hard window boundaries and isolated per-tenant buckets which causes wasted committed capacity and poor UX (throttles during predictable intra-day peaks). We need a safe mechanism to forward short-lived overspill (unused headroom) to sibling tenants within the reserved contract boundary and to permit soft-cap carryforward for the same tenant while preserving billing determinism and auditability. Goals: 1) Reduce visible throttling for tenants when capacity exists in the reserved pool, 2) Prevent systemic overconsumption that jeopardizes SLAs, 3) Keep metering and invoices deterministic and auditable, 4) Minimize latency and control-plane changes.
technical_design: Overview: Introduce an "overspill bucket" layer inside the reserved-pool quota controller that tracks transient unused capacity and exposes a time-limited borrow API. Key pieces: - Overspill bucket per-reserved-pool with two sub-buckets: tenant-forward (tenant-scoped carryforward up to configurable fraction) and pool-share (sibling borrowing weighted by reservation share). - Soft-cap enforcement: each tenant keeps its primary hard quota; when exhausted, the rate limiter will consult the overspill buckets and allow best-effort traffic subject to a proportional throttle rate computed as: allowed = min(remaining_pool_overspill * tenant_weight / pool_weight, max_burst_allowed). - TTL and decay: overspill credit decays linearly over a configurable window (default 6h) to avoid unbounded carryforwards. - Accounting: every borrow is emitted as two ledger records: provisional-usage and settled-usage. Settlement runs at end of tenant window (or on manual reconciliation) to convert provisional usage to billed units or roll it back when capacity constraints apply. - Safety: global circuit breaker that disables overspill forwarding when pool utilization exceeds a threshold (default 85%) and forces reversion to hard-rate limits. - Telemetry and trace context propagation for each borrow operation so we can attribute latency and cost to originating requests. - Minimal control plane change: runtime will consult the overspill allocator via existing quota-check RPC; allocator supports a new "borrow_hint" field and response codes for provisional_allow / provisional_deny. Trade-offs and rationale: - Complexity: introduces additional bookkeeping and settling logic; we balance this with strong observability and automatic auto-disable heuristics. - Billing determinism vs UX: provisional-usage makes immediate UX better at the cost of deferred settlement; we mitigate surprise by capping carryforward and surfacing provisional ledger items in the customer console. - Latency: a single additional in-process check when using the local allocator; for remote allocators we will batch borrow checks and cache results for very short windows. Implementation plan: 1) Library: implement allocator + ledger hooks in quota-service (go). 2) Runtime: wire borrow_hint in quota RPC and rate-limiter changes to consume provisional tokens. 3) UI: console surface for provisional usage and overspill credit balances. 4) Billing: pipeline job to settle provisional-usage into billed line items or create adjustment entries.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests covering overspill accounting, TTL decay, and circuit-breaker behavior
End-to-end demo: tenant A underutilizes quota, tenant B experiences burst and receives provisional capacity with correct ledger entries
No increase in p99 request latency > 4ms in quota path under normal load (benchmarks included)
Telemetry dashboards created: overspill-borrow-rate, provisional-to-settled conversion ratio, overspill-disabled-events
Rollout toggle implemented (feature flag) and rollback path validated
telemetry_and_metrics: New metrics: overspill.borrow_total, overspill.borrow_success, overspill.borrow_denied, overspill.settled_total, overspill.decayed_volume, overspill.disabled_count. Add tag dimensions: pool_id, tenant_id, route, reason. Create Grafana dashboard 'Reserved Pool Overspill' and an alert when overspill.disabled_count > 10 in 5m or when provisional_to_settled_ratio < 0.5 for 1h.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for allocator math, decay window, and safety gates. - Integration test harness simulating multiple tenants with synthetic traffic patterns to validate fairness and settlement. - Load test: compare existing quota path vs overspill-enabled path at 1000 qps per pool and measure latency/regression. - E2E billing dry-run where provisional usage is converted into a settlement stub (no invoice) to verify ledger correctness. - QA checklist includes console UX verification and manual checks for edge cases (DST boundaries, tenant timezone mismatches).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged rollout to internal staging pool for 48h. 2) Canary: enable for 5 low-risk customers (dedicated pools) for 7 days and monitor overspill metrics. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of reserved pools over 2 weeks. 4) Full opt-in toggle for customer admins via console (default off for new pools). 5) After 30 days evaluate impact and decide on opt-default policy. Emergency rollback: flip feature flag and run settlement flush job to reconcile provisional entries.
